intro: Identification of privacy legislation mentions in GitHub issues and Discussions of Hugging Face models and datasets.
pending: A dash indicates pending results. Pilots and simulated tests are excluded from scientific results.
method: Discovery precedes project selection. Confirmation records textual occurrences and their provenance; reviewers assign privacy categories.
cutoff: Inclusive cutoff: September 22, 2026, UTC. Missing or invalid dates do not establish eligibility. Current texts may include edits made after the cutoff.
github: GitHub: global search for legal terms in public closed issues; excludes pull requests and issues whose authors are identified as bots. A repository needs both an AI/ML discovery signal and technical evidence. Collection reads root manifests and the README when needed; source files and subdirectories are not traversed.
hf: Hugging Face: discovery of models and datasets under each OSI license; excludes Spaces, private and gated projects. A recognized task, pipeline or library in structured metadata confirms AI/ML. Only closed Discussions are accepted; authors identified as bots are excluded.
licenses: Both platforms: recognized SPDX license from the local OSI list and creation by the cutoff. Every identifier in a license expression must be approved. Forks and archived projects are accepted; there are no popularity thresholds.
concepts: 20 concepts: original and revised keyword lists from the replication package, matched with word boundaries and separate provenance. 24 categories: human codebook, without automatic keyword classification.
sampling: Strata: platform × repository type × law. Cochran with finite population correction: 99% confidence, 5% margin, 50% proportion; sample size rounded up and capped by population. Sampling without replacement uses base seed 20260920 plus stratum index.
coding: Each discussion appears once per reviewer in the CSV coding sheet, even if it belongs to several law strata. Two reviewers by default. Relevance: 0, 1 or blank. Categories: semicolon-separated codebook IDs without duplicates. Kappa uses complete pairs; no pairs or expected agreement of 1 yield an undefined result.
exports: CSV files for population, sample, strata, coding sheets and codebook, plus a hashed manifest, are stored in inputs/final/collection for subsequent analyses. Raw data and tokens are not copied to the website.
full: The --run option collects both platforms and analyzes a temporary database. The official database is replaced only after success, with archival of the previous one. Analysis verifies the latest attempts, unresolved problems, cutoff, versions and raw response hashes.
publication: The site is prepared for GitHub Pages. Publication uses a manual workflow. Local tests and rendering do not create commits or publish the project.
limits: Textual mentions do not establish legal compliance or violations. GitHub project totals refer to projects found through legal discussion searches, without estimating all AI/ML projects. Hugging Face discovery depends on license indexing. Pilots demonstrate a limited workflow; full coverage, duration and quota consumption require validation.
unfinished: BERT, human evaluation and all dissertation analyses are not run automatically. AI/ML selection accuracy and license coverage still require empirical validation.
rq_scope: GitHub versus Hugging Face is part of all three RQs. General OSS comparisons belong to RQ1 and RQ2. There is no RQ4 or before/after GDPR experiment. Automated comments on human-initiated discussions remain available as context.
rq3_instrument: Instrument ml-stages-1.0.0: model requirements, data collection, cleaning, labeling, feature engineering, training, evaluation, deployment and monitoring. This axis is separate from the 24 categories and inspired by Amershi et al. (2019). Operational definitions and LLM adaptations belong to this research; stages are not inferred from the hub.
rq3_review: Two reviewers independently cover the whole sample; consensus is stored in a separate sheet. Each identified stage requires an excerpt and its source artifact. Pending evaluation differs from indeterminate stage after evaluation. Stage agreement is computed before consensus; indeterminate or irrelevant pairs are not coded as stage absence.
rq3_denominator: Descriptions refer to the manual sample, without population extrapolation: N includes relevant discussions with completed stage assessment, including indeterminate ones. Pending assessments are separate. Multilabel proportions may sum to more than 100%. A zero denominator yields an undefined proportion; zero relevant HF discussions is a valid finding.
rq3_inference: For each of the nine stages: H0, relevant-discussion proportions are equal across hubs; H1, they differ. Contrasts require comparable projects, project clustering and cross-hub links, effects, intervals and Holm adjustment. Until these requirements are met, contrasts are recorded as not testable. Differences do not establish compliance or greater legal concern.
rq3_human_evaluation_pending: RQ3 pending: no actual stage annotations and consensus have been imported.
rq3_human_evaluation_partial: RQ3 partially annotated: reviews or consensus decisions are pending. Available descriptions are provisional.
rq3_human_evaluation_complete: RQ3: two independent assessments and consensus have been imported for the entire sample. Inferential contrasts still require an adequate study design.
no_collection: Scientific collection has not run yet.
collection_incomplete: The latest collections do not satisfy the protocol. Scientific results are pending.
analysis_pending: Collections completed. Run analysis to prepare the human evaluation sample.
ready_for_human_review: Collection and sampling completed. Human evaluation is pending; categories are not assigned automatically.
